shape: crit arm absent from the engine's branch support
signature: the observation carries |-crit| and its magnitude is ~2x the LARGEST any engine arm offers (measured ratios 2.13, 2.19, 2.05; a gen3 crit is exactly 2x)
method: source comparison, per the current program goal. Not signature profiling.

the_reference.behaviour: Sleep Talk picks a legal callee and runs `this.actions.useMove(randomMove, pokemon)` -- the ordinary move-execution path, which performs the normal critical-hit roll. gen3 has no sleeptalk override in data/mods/gen3/moves.ts, so base applies. A Sleep-Talk-called Ice Beam can crit at the usual 1/16.

the_engine.behaviour: for each callee it calls generate_instructions_from_move(..., false) -- the 7th parameter is branch_on_damage, hardcoded false. With branch_on_damage false the damage block at ~2830 takes its final `else { regular_damage = avg_damage_dealt }`, which emits NO crit arm. Both the Case A (straddling KO) and Case B (non-lethal crit) partitions are gated on branch_on_damage.
the_engine.consequence: a Sleep-Talk-called critical hit is REACHABLE IN THE SIMULATOR AND ABSENT FROM THE ENGINE'S SUPPORT.

worked_example.protocol: |move|p2a: Articuno|Sleep Talk -> |move|p2a: Articuno|Ice Beam|p1a: Seaking|[from] Sleep Talk, |-crit|, |-damage|p1a: Seaking|59/290
worked_example.arithmetic: 98 = 2 x 49; 46 is the 0.925 average of the non-crit roll. The crit arm at ~92 is simply not enumerated.

disposition.why_not_a_limit: this is precisely the fidelity objective's failure mode -- engine support must contain every reachable sim transition, and this transition is reachable and absent. It is not a branch-set-versus-sample artifact: the engine enumerates a branch set here and the crit member is missing from it.
disposition.why_not_a_matcher_fix: the matcher is correct to reject. There is no arm to match against.
disposition.the_fix: thread branch_on_damage through to the Sleep Talk recursive call instead of passing false.

pre_registered_prediction.falsifiable: these 3 rows match after the change, and the unattributed count on the 200-game window falls from 8 to 5.
pre_registered_prediction.invariants: no currently-matched row may become divergent; no registered family may grow.
pre_registered_prediction.cost_to_measure_BEFORE_shipping: Sleep Talk already fans out over N callees at 1/N mass each. Adding crit branching multiplies the callee subtree's branch count. The hardcoded false is plausibly a deliberate branch-count control, though it carries no comment saying so. Measure branch count and search throughput, and run the tactics suite, before this lands.

MEASURED.method: single-variable: the C87 patch is the only difference. #1021 and #1023 changed the readout and the contract, not the differential, so the sweep comparison is clean.
MEASURED.beyond_prediction: 19000065/123 also closed. c84 had filed it separately as 'crit present but ratio 1.40, not a clean doubling, separate cause'. It was the same cause: with the crit arm enumerated, the 1.40 ratio resolves against a crit roll the engine previously never offered. One shape, not two -- exactly the collapse the goal anticipates.

one_row_moved_INTO_unattributed.note: previously divergent-and-attributed, now divergent-and-unattributed. Net unattributed still falls 25 -> 22. Not closed by this change and not caused by it in the fidelity sense -- the engine's support grew, so a different arm now wins the comparison. Recorded as an open shape, NOT counted as a C87 win.
